questions.q: The sum of all possible values of $\theta \in[-\pi, 2 \pi]$, for which $\frac{1+i \cos \theta}{1-2 i \cos \theta}$ is purely imaginary, is equal
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & Z=\frac{1+i \cos \theta}{1-2 i \cos \theta} \\ & Z=-\bar{Z} \Rightarrow \frac{1+i \cos \theta}{1-2 i \cos \theta}=-\left(\frac{\overline{1+i \cos \theta}}{1-2 i \cos \theta}\right) \\ & (1+i \cos \theta)(\overline{1-2 i \cos \theta})=-(1-2 i \cos \theta)(\overline{1+i \cos \theta}) \\ & (1+i \cos \theta)(1+2 i \cos \theta)=-(1-2 i \cos \theta)(1-i \cos \theta) \\ & 1+3 i \cos \theta-2 \cos ^2 \theta=-\left(1-3 i \cos \theta-2 \cos ^2 \theta\right) \\ & 2-4 \cos ^2 \theta=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \cos ^2 \theta=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=-\frac{\pi}{4},-\frac{3 \pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{3 \pi}{4}, \frac{5 \pi}{4}, \frac{7 \pi}{4} \\ & \text { sum }=3 \pi\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $z$ be a complex number such that \left|\dfrac{z - 2i}{z + i}\right| = 2, z \ne - i$. Then $z$ lies on the circle of radius $2$ \text{ and } and centre$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given equation is

\left|\dfrac{z - 2i}{z + i}\right| = 2, z \ne - i$

On simplifying the equation, we get

$( z - 2i ) ( \overset{¯}{z} + 2i ) = 4 ( z + i ) ( \overset{¯}{z} - i )$

$⇒ z\overset{¯}{z} + 4 + 2i ( z - \overset{¯}{z} ) = 4 ( z\overset{¯}{z} + 1 + i ( \overset{¯}{z} - z ) )$

$⇒ 3z\overset{¯}{z} - 6i ( z - \overset{¯}{z} ) = 0$

Now putting the value of~$z = x + iy \text{ and } \overset{¯}{z} = x - iy$~we get,

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} - 2i ( 2iy ) = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} + 4y = 0$

On comparing the above equation with the general equation of the circle i.e

$( x - h{)}^{2} + ( y - k{)}^{2} = r^{2}$

We get, centre~$( 0, - 2 )$

$

If \left|z_1 \bar{z}_2+z_2 \bar{z}_3+z_3 \bar{z}_1\right|^2=\alpha+\beta \sqrt{2}, \alpha, \beta \in \mathbf{Z}$, then the value of $\alpha^2+\beta^2$ is :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & |z|=1 \\ & \arg \left(z_1\right)=-\frac{\pi}{4}, \arg \left(z_2\right)=0, \arg \left(z_3\right)=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ & z_1=|1| e^{-\frac{\pi}{4}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & z_2=1+0 i \\ & z_3=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & z_1 \bar{z}_2=\frac{1-i}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & z_2 \bar{z}_3=\frac{1-i}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & z_3 \bar{z}_1=\frac{(1+i)^2}{2} \\ & z_1 \bar{z}_2+z_2 \bar{z}_3+z_3 \bar{z}_1=\sqrt{2}+i(1-\sqrt{2}) \\ & \left|z_1 \bar{z}_2+z_2 \bar{z}_3+z_3 \bar{z}_1\right|^2=5-2 \sqrt{2} \\ & \alpha=5, \beta=-2 \\ & \alpha^2+\beta^2=29\end{aligned}$

${S}_{1} = { z \in \mathbb{C}: | z - 1 | \le \sqrt{2} } ,$

${S}_{2} = { z \in \mathbb{C}: Re ( ( 1 - i ) z ) \ge 1 }$~and

${S}_{3} = { z \in \mathbb{C}: Im ( z ) \le 1 } .$

Then, the set ${S}_{1} ∩ {S}_{2} ∩ {S}_{3}$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that the complex number& $z$~satisfying~\left|z - {z}_{0}\right| = r$~represents a circle with centre~${z}_{0}$~and radius~$r$~units.

Hence, for ${S}_{1} = | z - 1 | \le \sqrt{2}, z$ lies on and inside the circle
of radius $\sqrt{2}$ units and centre $( 1, 0 ) .$

For ${S}_{2},$~let~$z = x + iy$

Now,~$( 1 - i ) ( z ) = ( 1 - i ) ( x + iy )$

$⇒ ( 1 - i ) ( z ) = x + iy - ix - i^{2}y$

$⇒ ( 1 - i ) ( z ) = x + iy - ix + y$

$⇒ Re ( ( 1 - i ) z ) = x + y$

$⇒ x + y \ge 1 .$

And, for~${S}_{3},$~again let~$z = x + iy,$

$⇒ y \le 1 .$

Plotting all the inequalities on the graph, we get

Now, the common part is shown in the shaded part, hence, we get infinite points in the shaded region.

$⇒ {S}_{1} ∩ {S}_{2} ∩ {S}_{3}$ has infinitely many elements.

$

questions.q: Let $a, b$ be two real numbers such that $ab < 0$. If the complex number $\dfrac{1 + ai}{b + i}$ is of unit modulus and $a + ib$ lies on the circle \left|z - 1\right| =  \left|2z\right|$, then a possible value of \dfrac{1 + \left[a\right]}{4b},where \left[t\right] is greatest integer function, is :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$a, b$ be two real numbers such that $ab < 0$,~\left|\dfrac{1 + ai}{b + i}\right| = 1$,~$a + ib$ lies on the circle \left|z - 1\right| = \left|2z\right|$~and~$ab < 0$

Now using~\left|\dfrac{1 + ai}{b + i}\right| = 1$~we get,

$⇒ \left|1 + ai\right| = \left|b + i\right|$

Now squaring both side we get,

$⇒ \left|1 + ai\right|2 = \left|b + i\right|2$

$⇒ \left(1 + ai\right)\left(1 - ai\right) = \left(b + i\right)\left(b - i\right)\left\{\left|z\right|2 = z\overset{¯}{z}\right\}$

$⇒ 1 + a^{2} = b^{2} + 1$

$⇒ a = \pm b ⇒ b = - a$~as $ab < 0$

Now given,

\left(a, b\right)$ lies on \left|z - 1\right| = \left|2z\right|$

So,~\left|a + ib - 1\right| = 2\left|a + ib\right|$

$⇒ \left|a - 1 + ib\right|2 = 4 \left|a + ib\right|2$

$⇒ \left(a - 1\right)2 + b^{2} = 4\left(a^{2} + b^{2}\right)$

$⇒ \left(a - 1\right)2 + a^{2} = 4\left(2a^{2}\$right)\left$\{\text{as}$b = - a\right\}

$⇒ 6a^{2} + 2a - 1 = 0$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{- 2 \pm \sqrt{28}}{12} = \dfrac{- 1 \pm \sqrt{7}}{6}$

Taking positive sign we get,

$a = \dfrac{\sqrt{7} - 1}{6} \text{ and } b = \dfrac{1 - \sqrt{7}}{6}$~\left$\{\text{as}$b = - a\right\}

Now the value of~\left[$a\right] = 0$~as~$0 < \dfrac{\sqrt{7} - 1}{6} < 1$

$∴ \dfrac{1 + \left[$a\right]}{4b} = \dfrac{6}{4 \left($1 - $\sqrt{7}\right)} = - $\$left(\dfrac{1 + \sqrt{7}}{4}\right)

Now taking negative sign we get,~$a = $\dfrac{- 1 - \sqrt{7}}{6}$ \text{ and } b = $\dfrac{\sqrt{7} + 1}{6}

Now \left[a\right] = - 1\left\{\text{as} -1 < \dfrac{- 1 - \sqrt{7}}{6} < 0\right\}$

So, the value of~$\dfrac{1 + \left[a\right]}{4b} = \dfrac{1 + \left(- 1\right)}{4b} = \dfrac{0}{4b} = 0$

Note- Official answer key was drop by NTA, here we have modified the option.

$

Given $z = \dfrac{\alpha + i}{\alpha - i}$ , since $\alpha \in R$

$⇒ \left|z\right| = \left|\dfrac{\alpha + i}{\alpha - i}\right| = \left|\alpha + i\right|\left|\alpha - i\right|$

$⇒ \left|z\right| = 1$

Hence, locus of $z$ is a circle with radius $1$.

questions.q:
If the locus of $z \in \mathrm{C}$, such that
$\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z-1}{2 z+\mathrm{i}}\right)+\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{\bar{z}-1}{2 \bar{z}-\mathrm{i}}\right)=2$
is a circle of radius $r$ and center $(a, b)$ then $\frac{15 a b}{r^2}$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z-1}{2 z+i}\right)+\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{\bar{z}-1}{2 \bar{z}-i}\right)=2 \\ & \text { Here, } \frac{z-1}{2 z+i}=\left(\frac{\overline{\bar{z}-1}}{2 \bar{z}-i}\right)=2 \\ & =\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z-1}{2 z+i}\right)+\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{\mathrm{z}-1}{2 z+i}\right)=2 \\ & =2 \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z-1}{2 z+1}\right)=2 \Rightarrow \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z-1}{2 z+i}\right)=1
\end{aligned}$
Let $z=x+i y$
$\begin{aligned}
& \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{(x-1)+i y}{2 x+i(2 y+1)}\right)=1 \Rightarrow \operatorname{Re}\left[\frac{((x-1)+i y)(2 x-i(y+1)}{(2 x+i(2 y+1)(2 x-i(2 y+1))}\right]=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{2 x(x-1)+y(2 y+1)}{4 x^2+(2 y+1)^2}=1 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 x^2-2 x+2 y^2+y=4 x^2+4 y^2+1+4 y \\ & \Rightarrow 2 x^2+2 y^2+3 y+2 x+1=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x^2+y^2+x+\frac{3}{2} y+\frac{1}{2}=0 \\ & \text { centre }=\left(\frac{-1}{2}, \frac{-3}{4}\right), r=\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+\frac{9}{16}-\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{4} \\ & a=\frac{-1}{2}, b=\frac{-3}{4}, r^2=\frac{5}{16} \\ & 15 \frac{a b}{r^2}=15 \times\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right) \times\left(\frac{-3}{4}\right) \times \frac{16}{5}=18
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $S = \left\{z \in \mathbb{C}: \overset{¯}{z} = i\left(z^{2} + Re ( \overset{¯}{z} )\right)\right\}$. Then $\mathop{∑}_{z \in S} | z{|}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{¯}{z} = i \left(z^{2} + Re ( \overset{¯}{z} )\right)$

Now, let $z = x + iy$, so~$\overset{¯}{z} = x - iy$

Now putting the value in,~$\overset{¯}{z} = i \left(z^{2} + Re ( \overset{¯}{z} )\right)$~we get,

$\overset{¯}{z} = i \left(z^{2} + Re ( \overset{¯}{z} )\right)$

$⇒ x - iy = i \left($x^{2} - y^{2} + 2ixy + x\right)$

$⇒ x - iy = $i\left($x^{2} - y^{2} + x\right) - 2xy$

Now comparing real part we get,

$⇒ x = - 2xy ⇒ x ( 2y + 1 ) = 0$

$⇒ x = 0, y = $\dfrac{- 1}{2} . . . . . \left($1\right)$

And imaginary part we get,

$- y = x^{2} - y^{2} + x . . . . . . . \left($2\right)$

Now taking~Case (I) when~$x = 0$~in~equation~ \left($2\right)$~we get,

$⇒ - y = - y^{2}$

$⇒ y^{2} - y = 0 ⇒ y = 0, 1$

So,~$z = 0, i$

Now taking Case (II) when~$y = $\dfrac{- 1}{2}~in equation~ \left(2\right)$~we get,

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{2} =$x^{2} - $\dfrac{1}{4} +$x$

$⇒ x^{2} + x - $\dfrac{3}{4} =$0$

$⇒ 4x + 4x - 3 = 0$

$⇒ ( 2x - 1 ) ( 2x + 3 ) = 0$

$⇒ x = $\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{- 3}{2}

So,~$z = $\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}$i, $\dfrac{- 3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}$i$

Now finding,~$∑ | z{|}^{2} = 0 + 1 + $\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{5}{2} =$4$

$

questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $2 z^2-3 z-2 \mathrm{i}=0$, where $\mathrm{i}=\sqrt{-1}$, then $16 \cdot \operatorname{Re}\$left(\frac{\alpha^{19}+\beta^{19}+\alpha^{11}+\beta^{11}}{\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15}}\right) \cdot \operatorname{lm} $\$left(\frac{\alpha^{19}+\beta^{19}+\alpha^{11}+\beta^{11}}{\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15}}\right)is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$2 z^2-3 z-2 i=0$ ...(i)
$2\left(z-\frac{i}{z}\right)=3$
As $\alpha, \beta$ are roots of (i)
$\begin{aligned}
& \alpha-\frac{i}{\alpha}=\frac{3}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \alpha^2-\frac{1}{\alpha^2}-2 i=\frac{9}{4} \\
& \Rightarrow \alpha^2-\frac{1}{\alpha^2}=\frac{9}{4}+2 i
\end{aligned}$ Squaring both sides
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \alpha^4+\frac{1}{\alpha^4}-2=\frac{81}{16}-4+9 i \\
& \Rightarrow \alpha^4+\frac{1}{\alpha^4}=\frac{49}{16}+9 i
\end{aligned}$ Similarly, $\beta^4+\frac{1}{\beta^4}=\frac{49}{16}+9 i\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\alpha^{19}+\beta^{19}+\alpha^{11}+\beta^{11}}{\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15}} \\
& =\frac{\alpha^{15}\left(\alpha^4+\frac{1}{\alpha^4}\right)+\beta^{15}\left(\beta^4+\frac{1}{\beta^4}\right)}{\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15}} \\
& =\frac{49}{16}+9 i \\
& \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{\alpha^{19}+\beta^{19}+\alpha^{11}+\beta^{11}}{\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15}}\right)=\frac{49}{16} \\
& \operatorname{Im}\left(\frac{\alpha^{19}+\beta^{19}+\alpha^{11}+\beta^{11}}{\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15}}\right)=9 \\
& \Rightarrow 16 \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{\alpha^{19}+\beta^{19}+\alpha^{11}+\beta^{11}}{\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15}}\right) \cdot \operatorname{lm}\left(\frac{\alpha^{19}+\beta^{19}+\alpha^{11}+\beta^{11}}{\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15}}\right) \\
& =16 \times \frac{49}{16} \times 9 \\
& =441
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If the center and radius of the circle  \left|\dfrac{z - 2}{z - 3}\right| = 2$ are respectively \left(\alpha, \beta\right)$ and $\gamma$, then $3  \left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right)$is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given:

\left|\dfrac{z - 2}{z - 3}\right| = 2$

Let~$z = x + iy$, then we have

\left|\dfrac{x - 2 + iy}{x - 3 + iy}\right| = 2$

$⇒ \sqrt{\left(x - 2\right)2 + y^{2}} = 2\sqrt{\left(x - 3\right)2 + y^{2}}$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 4 = 4x^{2} + 4y^{2} - 24x + 36$

$⇒ 3x^{2} + 3y^{2} - 20x + 32 = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} - \dfrac{20}{3}x + \dfrac{32}{3} = 0$

So,~ \left(\alpha, \beta\right) ≡ \left(\dfrac{10}{3},0\right)$

And,

$\gamma = \sqrt{\dfrac{100}{9} - \dfrac{32}{3}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{9}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Therefore,

$3\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) ==3\$left(\dfrac{10}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3}\right) =12$

$

questions.q: If the real part of the complex number $z = \dfrac{3 + 2icos\theta}{1 - 3icos\theta}, \theta \in  \left($0, \dfrac{π}{2}\right)$is zero, then the value of $\sin^{2}3\theta + \cos^{2}\thetais$equal to ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$We have,& $z = \dfrac{3 + 2icos\theta}{1 - 3icos\theta}, \theta \in \left($0, $\dfrac{π}{2}\right)

$⇒ z = $\dfrac{3 + 2icos\theta}{1 - 3icos\theta} \times \dfrac{1 + 3icos\theta}{1 + 3icos\theta}

$⇒ z = $\dfrac{\left(3 + 2icos\theta\right)\left(1 + 3icos\theta\right)}{1 + 9\cos^{2}\theta}

$⇒ z = \left($3 - 6\cos^{2}$\theta +$11icos$\theta\right)$1 + 9\cos^{2}$\theta

Now,~$Re \left($z\right) = $\dfrac{3 - 6\cos^{2}\theta}{1 + 9\cos^{2}\theta} =$0$

$⇒ 3 - 6\cos^{2}$\theta =$0$

$⇒ \cos^{2}$\theta = \dfrac{3}{6}

$⇒ \cos^{2}$\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}

$⇒ cos$\theta = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}

$⇒ $\theta = \dfrac{π}{4},$∵ $\theta \in \left($0, $\dfrac{π}{2}\right)

Hence, \sin^{2}3\theta + \cos^{2}\theta

$= \sin^{2} \left(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right) + \cos^{2} \left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right)$

$= $\l$left(sin \left(\pi - $\dfrac{π}{4}\right)\right)2 + $\l$left(cos \left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right)\right)$2$

$= $\l$left(sin $\$left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right)\right)2 + $\l$left(cos \left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right)\right)$2 = 1$

Since,~\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta =$1$

$

questions.q: If $\alpha$ satisfies the equation $x^{2} + x + 1 = 0$ and $( 1 + \alpha{)}^{7} = A + B\alpha + C{α}^{2}, A, B, C \ge 0$, then $5 ( 3A - 2B - C )$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that, $1 + \omega + {ω}^{2} = 0$.

So, the roots of the equation $x^{2} + x + 1 = 0$ are $\omega$ and ${ω}^{2}$.

Let, $\alpha = \omega$

$⇒ \left(1 + \alpha\right)7 = \left(1 + \omega\right)7$

$⇒ \left(1 + \alpha\right)7 = \left(- {ω}^{2}\right)7$

$⇒ \left(1 + \alpha\right)7 = - {ω}^{14}$

We know that, ${ω}^{3n} = 1$.

$⇒ \left(1 + \alpha\right)7 = - {ω}^{2} = 1 + \omega$

Now, on comparing with equation we get,

$⇒ A = 1, B = 1, C = 0$

$⇒ 5 \left(3A - 2B - C\right) = 5 \left($3 - 2 - 0\right)$

$⇒ $5\left($3A - 2B - C\right) = 5$

$

questions.q:
Let& $\alpha = 8 - 14i, A = \left\{z \in \mathbb{C}: \dfrac{\alphaz - \overset{¯}{α}\overset{¯}{z}}{z^{2} - ( \overset{¯}{z}{)}^{2} - 112i} = 1\right\}$~and~$B = \left\{z \in \mathbb{C}: \left|z + 3i\right| = 4\right\}$

Then,~$\mathop{∑}_{z \in A ∩ B} ( Re z - Imz )$& & is equal to& ________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$A = \left\{z \in \mathbb{C}: \dfrac{\alphaz - \overset{¯}{α}\overset{¯}{z}}{z^{2} - ( \overset{¯}{z}{)}^{2} - 112i} = 1\right\}$

$B = \left\{z \in \mathbb{C}: \left|z + 3i\right| = 4\right\}$

$\alpha = 8 - 14i$

Let

$z = x + iy$

So,

$\alphaz = \left(8 - 14i\right) \left($x + iy\right)$

$⇒ \alphaz = ( 8x + 14y ) + i ( - 14x + 8y )$

Also,

$z + \overset{¯}{z} = 2x$~and~$z - \overset{¯}{z} = 2iy$

Set A:

\dfrac{\alphaz - \overset{¯}{α}\overset{¯}{z}}{z^{2} - ( \overset{¯}{z}{)}^{2} - 112i} =$1$

$⇒ $\dfrac{2i\left(- 14x + 8y\right)}{\left(z + \overset{¯}{z}\right)\left(z - \overset{¯}{z}\right) - 112i} =$1$

$⇒ $\dfrac{2i\left(- 14x + 8y\right)}{4ixy - 112i} =$1$

~$⇒ - 14x + $8y\left($2xy - 56\right) = 1$

$⇒ xy + 7x - 4y - 28 = 0$

$⇒ \left($x - 4\right)\left(y + 7\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = 4$~or~$y = - 7$

Set~$B$:

\left|z + 3i\right| = 4$

$⇒ \left|x + i\left(y + 3\right)\right| = 4$

$⇒ x^{2} + \left(y + 3\right)2 = 16$

When~$x = 4 ⇒ y = - 3$

When~$y = - 7 ⇒ x = 0$

$∴ A ∩ B = \left\{4 - 3i, 0 - 7i\right\}$

So,~$\mathop{∑}_{z \in A ∩ B}\left(Rez - Im z\right) = 4 - ( - 3 ) + ( 0 - ( - 7 ) ) = 14$

$

questions.q: Sum of squares of modulus of all the complex numbers& $z$ satisfying $\overset{¯}{z} = iz^{2} + z^{2} - z$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$z + \overset{¯}{z} = {izz}^{2} + z^{2}$

Consider~$z = x + iy$

$2x = \left(i + 1\right) \left($x^{2} - y^{2} + 2xyi\right)$

On comparing real and imaginary part we get,

$⇒ 2x = x^{2} - y^{2} - 2xy$~and~$x^{2} - y^{2} + 2xy = 0$

$⇒ 2x = - 4xy$

$⇒ x = 0$~or~$y = $\dfrac{- 1}{2}

Case 1:~$x = 0 ⇒ 2 \times0 = \left($i + 1\right)\left({0}^{2} -y^{2} + 2 \times0 \timesyi\right)y = 0$~

Here~$z = 0$

Case 2:~$y = $\dfrac{- 1}{2}

$⇒ 4x^{2} - 4x - 1 = 0$

\left(2x - 1\right)2 = 2$

$2x - 1 = \pm $\sqrt{2}

$x = $\dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{2}}{2}

Here~$z = $\dfrac{1 + \sqrt{2}}{2} - \dfrac{i}{2}~or~$z = $\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{2}}{2} - \dfrac{i}{2}

Sum of squares of modulus of~$z$

$= 0 + $\dfrac{\left(1 + \sqrt{2}\right)2 + 1}{4} + \dfrac{\left(1 - \sqrt{2}\right)2 + 1}{4} = \dfrac{8}{4} =$2$

$
